item.title: Climate & French fries
item.description: Warmer conditions will pose new challenges for producers of Americans’ favorite side dish but advance knowledge and innovation will help potato growers prepare.

item.title: Climate & skiing
item.description: From retreating snow elevations to rain-soaked powder, warming due to human-caused climate change will radically transform U.S. skiing over the remainder of the twenty-first century.
item.dc:creator: Michon Scott

item.title: Climate & allergies
item.description: Hay fever might leave you wanting to live north of that Westeros Wall, but the farther north you live in the contiguous United States, the worse your allergies may get in a warming climate.
item.dc:creator: Michon Scott

item.title: Climate & construction
item.description: Can climate science help the construction industry save money and manage risk?  With a new app, a team of scientists and construction managers aims to find out.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Freeman

item.title: Climate and human evolution
item.description: Rick Potts of the Smithsonian Institution discusses the role of climate variation in the evolution of our ancestors.
item.dc:creator: Michon Scott

item.title: Climate and mummies
item.description: The world's oldest mummies have been infected with a destructive black ooze. Climate change may be responsible.
item.dc:creator: Emily Greenhalgh

item.title: Climate & Chocolate
item.description: Over the next several decades, cacao-growing regions may grow warmer and drier, but with planning and adaptation, farmers can keep producing our favorite treat.
